dedupe_keys.name: netl national critical minerals data dashboard

description: The Critical Minerals Data Dashboard from the National Energy Technology Laboratory gives an interactive map and filters over data on conventional and unconventional critical mineral resources in the United States, focused on 12 critical minerals needed for zero-emission transport and clean power technology. The EDX and DataCite pages say the datasets were compiled from the USGS, the US EPA, the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) and the Department of Homeland Security, can be filtered by geography along the top of the dashboard and by attributes in a side panel, and are explained further in a companion critical minerals story map. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY (version not stated; NETL EDX lists 'Creative Commons Attribution'). Access is free of charge. Coverage is national. Caveats: the list of the 12 minerals and of the layers behind the dashboard is not stated on the pages read, and dashboard views can change without versioning. For simulation it helps locate domestic critical mineral sources, including unconventional ones such as coal wastes and mine drainage, for supply chain resilience and siting scenarios. Related catalogue records include the NEWTS integrated energy wastewater dataset, the USGS Critical mineral deposits of the United States and the USGS Mineral Resources Data System.
